input: Convert /data/employees.json (an array of objects with keys name, department, salary) to CSV format with a header row. Save the result to /data/employees.csv and print it. The output should have the header 'name,department,salary' followed by one data row per object.

transcript.final_response:
I converted the JSON to CSV and saved it to `/data/employees.csv`. It has the header `name,department,salary` and one row for each of the 4 employees:

```
name,department,salary
Alice Chen,Engineering,120000
Bob Park,Marketing,95000
Carol Wu,Engineering,115000
Dave Kim,Sales,88000
```

I used `jq` to pull the three fields out of each object. My first try put quotes around every text value, which is valid CSV but harder to read, so I redid it. Now a value only gets quotes if it contains a comma, a double quote or a line break, and any double quotes inside it are doubled. None of the current values need this, so the file has no quotes in it.
tool_calls: { echo "name,department,salary"; jq -r '.[] | [.name, .department, .salary] | map(tostring | if test("[,\"\n]") then "\"" + gsub("\""; "\"\"") + "\"" else . end) | join(",")' /data/employees.json; } > /data/employees.csv; cat /data/employees.csv
